description: Bugs/issues discovered by harness task agents. Distinct from the earlier build/consumer loop/fix_queue.md (F1-F22).

items.title: Operator UI panel exists but is not integrated into a running dashboard or UI-tested
items.detail: packages/pack-loyalty/src/ui/LoyaltyOperatorPanel.tsx exists and typechecks (and was de-corrupted in T9e — a stray </content> tag was stripped), but it is only barrel-exported, not wired into a running operator dashboard and has no UI test. The module_acceptance_checklist 'Operator UI' box (list/detail/issue/redeem) is therefore only partially met; loyalty was certified reference-tier on the backend/SDK/docs surfaces with this recorded as an exception.
items.impact: Loyalty has no demonstrable operator UI flow yet; G10 only partially closed for loyalty.
items.recommended_fix: Wire LoyaltyOperatorPanel into the operator dashboard (list programs/accounts, issue/earn, redeem/consume/revoke, audit trail) and add a UI test.
items.resolution: T15: shipped a NATIVE operator dashboard in the console — ui/src/pages/LoyaltyConsole.tsx (route /loyalty + nav) covering connect / setup / overview / earn / redeem / consume / revoke / RightAction receipt / ledger evidence / dev snippet, on the real client.loyalty.* via a lazy @tokenisation/sdk import. UI test ui/src/tests/loyalty/LoyaltyConsole.test.tsx (1/1) asserts the flow + idempotency key. Built native rather than importing pack-loyalty/src/ui/LoyaltyOperatorPanel.tsx because that panel is excluded from pack-loyalty's build (react not a runtime dep) so it is not importable from the built package; the pack panel remains a portable reference component. Verifier PASS (T15 loyalty-dashboard sub-goal).

items.title: Console vitest suite is red — crypto-browserify is not installed
items.detail: ui/vitest.config.ts aliases 'crypto' -> src/mocks/crypto-shim.ts, which imports 'crypto-browserify' (not installed). Any test whose import graph reaches node 'crypto' (the SDK umbrella) fails to load: 16 pre-existing failures across store-api, uikit-sdk-integration, uikit-demo-smoke. Proven pre-existing (fails with the T15 edits stashed). The new LoyaltyConsole test avoids it by lazy-importing the SDK only on connect.
items.impact: Console test suite cannot run end-to-end; CI signal for ui/ is broken. ALSO blocked `pnpm dev` (the vite app aliases crypto->crypto-shim too), so the console could not boot at all.
items.recommended_fix: Install crypto-browserify (devDep) OR point the crypto-shim at an installed polyfill / Node's built-in webcrypto. Part of T15 'stabilize UI + tests'.
items.resolution: Installed crypto-browserify as a console devDep (the vite/vitest crypto-shim already referenced it). The console dev server now boots clean on http://localhost:5173. Discovered while running the loyalty dashboard.

items.title: Pre-existing console typecheck debt (tsconfig.app.json not clean)
items.detail: tsc -p ui/tsconfig.app.json reports pre-existing errors unrelated to loyalty: ComputeDemo.tsx:521 (status union), blueprints/ProgressStepper.tsx:48 (string|undefined), core/store.ts:27 + store.ts:17 (Cannot find module '@tokenisation/sdk/plugins'), integrate/LogsPage.tsx:599/630 (unknown not assignable to ReactNode), routes.tsx:65 (<Dashboard/> missing required onSelectAsset). The T15 loyalty files add zero new errors. So build:typecheck (tsc && vite build) is red independent of this work.
items.impact: Console does not typecheck-build clean; masks new type regressions.
items.recommended_fix: Clear these in the T15 stabilize-UI sweep (or a dedicated typecheck-debt task).
items.resolution: The two BOOT-BLOCKING errors are fixed: store.ts:17 + core/store.ts:27 imported '@tokenisation/sdk/plugins', a subpath declared in the sdk exports map but NEVER built (the sdk build emits only the bundled root) — redirected both to the main barrel '@tokenisation/sdk' (ApiClient/ApiStoragePlugin/ApiEventStore are re-exported there), which unblocks the console boot. STILL OPEN: the other pre-existing type errors (ComputeDemo.tsx:521, ProgressStepper.tsx:48, LogsPage.tsx:599/630, routes.tsx:65 <Dashboard/> onSelectAsset) and the ROOT sdk-packaging bug — the exports map declares subpaths (./plugins, ./components, ./core, ./models, ...) whose dist is never produced by the sdk build (reroute the packaging fix to T16). The /components reference in ui is only example text in a template string, not a real import.

items.title: vite dev hits ENOSPC (inotify watch limit) on this host
items.detail: `pnpm dev` for the console crashes with ENOSPC (syscall: 'watch') because fs.inotify.max_user_watches is exhausted on this machine. Worked around by running with CHOKIDAR_USEPOLLING=true (chokidar polls instead of using inotify). Host/env limit, not a code bug.
items.impact: Dev server won't start with the native watcher on this host.
items.recommended_fix: Either raise the OS limit (sudo sysctl fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288) or set server.watch.usePolling in vite.config / document CHOKIDAR_USEPOLLING=true.

items.title: Loyalty programs/accounts list+get not exposed (no server routes)
items.detail: The SDK loyalty surface only exposes methods backed by T9c routes: programs.create, accounts.create, points.*, transactions.list. The module-contract 'preferred shape' also lists programs.list/get and accounts.get/list, but T9c added no such routes. Add GET routes (programs list/get, account get/list) + SDK methods in T9e or a T9c extension.
items.impact: Developers cannot list/get programs or fetch an account by id via SDK yet.
items.recommended_fix: Add server GET routes + SDK methods; cover with tests.
items.note: Deliberately NOT done in T9e: the module_acceptance_checklist 'Surfaces' boxes do not require list/get, and the recipe documents this as a known limitation. Re-routed off T9e (which is done) to backlog; fold into a loyalty surface-completion task or T13 (curate public SDK surface).

items.title: T9a spec assumed a new FIFO ledger; existing server loyalty.service uses account-balance
items.detail: docs/modules/loyalty.module.md (T9a) described a new FIFO loyalty_balances ledger and 'no server service', but server/src/services/loyalty.service.ts already exists (loyalty_programs/accounts/transactions, account-balance). T9b integrated with the existing service instead (D-13). The module spec's §4/§8 FIFO-batch wording should be updated to the account-balance model in T9e.
items.impact: Spec doc slightly ahead of implementation reality; reconcile in T9e docs pass.
items.recommended_fix: Update loyalty.module.md to the account-balance model during T9e.
items.resolution: Reconciled in T9e: docs/modules/loyalty.module.md §2/§4 and docs/recipes/LOYALTY_POINTS.md describe the account-balance model and explicitly state 'not a FIFO loyalty_balances ledger'. Verified by the verifier agent.

items.title: Ledger decrement + RightAction creation are not in one DB transaction
items.detail: spendViaRight decrements the ledger (spendPoints) then createAction. Pre-checks (balance, idempotency) make a mid-failure unlikely, but there is no cross-table atomicity. Consider wrapping in a DB transaction or an outbox.
items.impact: Rare partial-state risk under concurrent/failure conditions.
items.recommended_fix: Wrap spend+action in a transaction (or reconcile via outbox) in a later hardening pass.

items.title: Duplicate ValidationError classes — one does not extend SDKError
items.detail: Two classes named ValidationError exist: packages/core/src/errors/index.ts:187 (extends SDKError — intended public error) and packages/core/src/modules/validation.ts:661 (extends Error — does NOT extend SDKError). The root barrel (packages/core/src/index.ts) re-exports the errors-module one explicitly (line 227, with a 'takes precedence' comment) while also `export *`-ing modules. Correct ES semantics make the explicit re-export win, but this is fragile: a consumer importing ValidationError via a different path (e.g. a deep import of modules/validation) gets the Error-only variant, so `err instanceof SDKError` / `isSDKError(err)` would be false. Surfaced as cross-barrel instanceof failures in the first test run.
items.impact: Latent: error-type checks (isSDKError / instanceof SDKError) can silently fail depending on import path. Relevant to T3 (unify error model).
items.recommended_fix: Rename or remove the modules/validation.ts ValidationError (make it extend SDKError, or alias to the errors one). Not done in T1 (not tiny/isolated; touches a public-ish export). Fold into T3 (unify error model + error-code catalog).

items.title: API keys do not carry role permissions — provision scopes from roles
items.detail: createApiKey defaults scopes to ['read','write'] (iam.service:429) and keys are not linked to the rich DEFAULT_ROLES permissions. The matcher now understands role-permission strings, but keys never receive them, so resource-level authz (write:compliance vs write:tokens) is not actually differentiated in production unless callers set custom scopes. Wire key issuance to a role (or accept explicit permission strings) so a 'compliance_officer' key gets ['read:*','write:compliance','write:kyc'].
items.impact: Until done, all real keys are effectively coarse read/write; resource-level guards added later won't discriminate.
items.recommended_fix: New task: link apiKeys -> role(s); populate scopes from role permissions on issuance.

items.title: Roll out resource-level requireScope across the 48 routers
items.detail: requireScope now supports requireScope(action, resource) but routes still call the coarse form (e.g. requireScope('write')). To get real per-resource authz, routes should declare their resource: tokens -> requireScope('write','tokens'), compliance -> requireScope('write','compliance'), etc. Mechanical but broad; do as a reviewed sweep, not in T2.
items.impact: Resource-level enforcement is available but not yet applied; coarse guards remain in place (safe, just not granular).
items.recommended_fix: New task: annotate each router's mutations with its resource.

items.title: Insufficient-permission should be 403, not 401
items.detail: requireScope throws UnauthorizedError (401) when an authenticated key lacks a permission; semantically that is 403 Forbidden. Kept 401 in T2 for compatibility (clients/tests may depend on it). Revisit with the error-model unification.
items.impact: Minor API-correctness; could confuse clients distinguishing authn vs authz failures.

items.title: Land USAGE/LICENSE in the RightType enum + introduce RightProfile (T5a)
items.detail: T5 ratified USAGE (consumable/metered) and LICENSE (terms-bound/revocable) as canonical RightTypes and the two-level RightType+RightProfile model, but did NOT add them to packages/core/src/core/types.ts RightType enum (no current code uses them; future modules deferred). Add them additively when the first consuming module's spec is accepted, introduce the RightProfile type (attributes: transferable/divisible/expires/revocable/delegable/consumable), and optionally tighten PackManifest.rightTypes to validate against the enum. Update the core taxonomy-stability test (it asserts USAGE/LICENSE are NOT yet members — intentional change-detector).
items.impact: Until landed, compute-credit/license modules cannot set a canonical rightType; they would carry pending profiles. Additive/low-risk (no exhaustive switches).
items.recommended_fix: Implement as task T5a, gated to first consuming module.

items.title: Implement the Right Action primitive (T6a/T6b/T6c)
items.detail: T6 ratified the design (harness/redemption_consumption_primitive.md). Implementation is broad and split into: T6a — core RightActionService + right_actions table/migration + status machine + balance handling + audit/idempotency wiring + conformance tests (§9); T6b — server API (POST /api/v1/rights/actions + history + receipt) + OpenAPI + RBAC guards + back-compat shims for /tokens/:id/redeem and /redemptions/*; T6c — SDK client.rights.* surface + types + tests. First consumer is T9 (loyalty), which retires the in-memory redeem(). Securities redemption migrates onto the primitive under a T10 follow-up. Primitive keys off RightProfile attributes (not T5a); policy gating (T7) and metadata validation (T8) are referenced deps.
items.impact: Until built, redemption stays fragmented (G8). T9 cannot proceed without T6a (its core dependency).
items.recommended_fix: Execute T6a -> T6b -> T6c; verify with conformance tests; integrate in T9.

items.title: rawQuery/execStatement forbid reusing a $n placeholder
items.detail: config/database.ts rawQuery converts each $n -> ? textually, so reusing a numbered placeholder (e.g. created_at=$14, updated_at=$14, or completed_at=$3 twice) yields more ? than bound values -> 'Too few parameter values were provided' on sqlite. Use distinct $n and pass the value multiple times. Guidance for T6b and any raw-SQL service.
items.impact: Authoring footgun only; caught + fixed in T6a.
items.recommended_fix: Documented; consider a helper that supports named/repeated params later.

items.title: Right Action core has no balance ledger / policy / metadata validation
items.detail: The core records CONSUME quantity but does not decrement a balance (module-owned ledger lands in T9 for loyalty). No policy gating (POLICY_DENIED -> T7) and no per-RightProfile metadata validation (T8) yet. Also no HTTP routes (T6b) or SDK surface (T6c).
items.impact: T9 must supply the loyalty balance ledger and wire CONSUME/REDEEM through this core.
items.recommended_fix: T6b (routes), T6c (SDK), T9 (loyalty balance + integration), T7/T8 when ready.

items.title: Cross-barrel instanceof is brittle under vite source loading
items.detail: Importing the full root barrel (../src/index.js) in vitest can dual-instantiate modules (large barrel + circular imports), so `factory() instanceof BarrelApiClient` can be false even though it is an ApiClient. Not a shipped bug (the built dist is a single module graph). Foundation tests assert same-module identity + behavioral contract instead.
